correctness.rationale: Checked the inverse of the compressed resolvent, not the compression of A. In the Krylov basis with first vector b/||b||, the off-diagonal of J is the positive standard deviation of r_i under b_i² weights, giving distinct nodes. Equality of a Ritz node with a spectral endpoint would require a nonzero affine function of r_i to vanish at the other two distinct levels. Affine exactness gives the coordinate multiplier as the two-node interpolant of exp[−t(r⁻¹−1)/γ]; its positive slope for t>0 and the sign test at r_min establish the global first crossing, including ties in the largest decay rate. The one- and two-level invariant cases are exact. A separate symbolic moment-pencil calculation in the basis {b,Db} gives the limiting resolvent characteristic polynomial x²−(10/21)x+1/84 and horizon 0.079671742512472362. For D=A_L the same pencil gives, after x=L−h/L, the characteristic polynomial 1/2−h+O(1/L); at x=3/2−h/L it gives h−1/2+O(1/L). These yield the stated root expansions and the logarithm 2 log L+O(1) in the polynomial horizon. The supplied floating-point checks are only corroboration.
residual_risks: Exact arithmetic; the positive limiting horizon is at fixed unit shift in the specified family, not a bound uniform over all families or shifts.

evidence: Apply the earlier horizon theorem with eigenvalues 1−r_i and Ritz nodes 1−η_+, 1−η_−. After division by α the threshold is exactly the submitted T_γ, with the same maximal-rate crossing. Neither inspected source supplies the limiting compressed-resolvent Ritz polynomial with two positive nondegenerate nodes or the distinct endpoint asymptotics for A_L.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The unrestricted threshold formula is covered as a corollary. Establishing the stiff separation requires additional spectral asymptotics: one Ritz pair stays interior and separated for the transformed family, while the untransformed upper Ritz node has a gap ∼1/(2L) from L. This is not a substitution of fixed data into a previously stated stiff-limit theorem.

evidence: The published shift-and-invert algorithm uses exactly the inverse of the compressed resolvent. Set D=I−R. Then the polynomial Krylov subspace for D is the same subspace, and its compression is I−J. In two dimensions H=cI+α(I−J), with α=1/(γη_+η_−)>0, by matching its two eigenvalues.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For signs the scalar factor exp(−ct) is immaterial. The universal sign law is equivalent to polynomial Lanczos on D at time αt, and the exact threshold follows by rescaling. The novel comparison is instead against polynomial Lanczos on A, not on D.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is the explicit noncollapsing stiff-limit witness and its unbounded ratio against the polynomial horizon on the same original operator. Neither the shift-and-invert algorithm nor the universal two-node sign law in isolation is credited as new: the latter is a direct time-rescaled consequence of the earlier polynomial sign theorem on a transformed operator. The Finding and prior-work section emphasize the stiff-limit comparison, which was not covered by the sources checked.
residual_risks: The focused general search was inconclusive, and the Druskin full text was unavailable. An earlier explicit separation under an equivalent formulation remains possible.
The universal horizon alone would not pass originality as a separate finding.

value.rationale: A concrete stiffness counterexample distinguishes positivity failure of two established approximations applied to the same diagonal system. Ordinary Lanczos loses positivity on a time scale tending to zero, but the compressed-resolvent projection retains a quantifiable positive window without preserving positivity forever. This addresses a property not measured by general error estimates; the universal threshold by itself is a reformulation, not the main value.
residual_risks: No error superiority, positivity-preserving solver, or result for general dimensions of the projection is asserted.
